summary: @alphaspace/core exfiltrates installer host metadata to hardcoded Pipedream webhook via preinstall/postinstall
details: package.json declares both preinstall and postinstall to run `node collect.js`. collect.js gathers installer host identifiers — os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), process.platform/arch, Node version, npm registry configuration, present CI environment variable names, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, and DNS lookup results for internal Yahoo hostnames — base64-encodes the payload and POSTs it via https.request to the hardcoded endpoint https://7f7a3ffb0c812f2be7786eb430522c59.m.pipedream.net. Version 99.0.3 combined with an otherwise empty package (`index.js` exports `{}`) matches the dependency-confusion shape: the high version wins resolution against a lower-versioned internal `@alphaspace/core` and executes the collector on any host that resolves the name from the public registry. The package labels itself a bug-bounty proof-of-concept, but the install-time reconnaissance beacon fires against every installer regardless of whether they are party to the researcher's engagement, and the destination is a third-party author-controlled webhook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
